title: "Clinical background"
format: html
---

Cryptococcosis is the third most common invasive fungal disease in organ transplant recipients, and carries substantial mortality [@yoon2022antibody].

Two kinds of antibody are relevant to *Cryptococcus neoformans*:

-   **Glucuronoxylomannan (GXM)-binding antibodies** recognize the main component of the fungal polysaccharide capsule.
-   **Laminarin (Lam)-binding antibodies** recognize laminarin, a β-glucan from the brown alga *Laminaria digitata* that stands in for the β-(1-3)-glucan of the fungal cell wall [@torosantucci2005lam].

Both have been associated with cryptococcosis status or risk in people with and without HIV infection [@yoon2022antibody]. In transplant recipients, Jalali et al. found pretransplant GXM-IgM lower, but posttransplant GXM-IgM and IgG higher, in patients who developed cryptococcosis [@jalali2006gxm]. This study measured both antibodies, together with total (non-specific) IgM, IgG1 and IgG2, in transplant recipients with and without a history of posttransplant cryptococcosis [@yoon2022antibody].

## Study design in brief

-   **Setting:** University of Alabama at Birmingham; recruitment 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2018.
-   **Cases:** organ transplant recipients with a history of posttransplant cryptococcosis, diagnosed by a positive cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) test or body fluid culture.
-   **Controls:** organ transplant recipients with no such history.
-   **Measurements:** serum total IgM, IgG1 and IgG2 (µg/mL, Luminex); GXM- and Lam-binding IgM and IgG (titers); serum CrAg by lateral flow assay.
-   **Approvals:** the UAB Institutional Review Board approved the study, all patients gave written informed consent, and the samples were studied under an Albert Einstein College of Medicine IRB-approved protocol.

See [`analysis-plan.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/analysis-plan.md) for the full specification.
